title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #208
gist: A roundup of six positive-sum tech/science developments: a fast-tracked pancreatic cancer drug from Revolution Medicines, a $37M raise for drone startup Airbound, two nuclear microreactor startups (Radiant and Antares) landing a $2.2B US Army program, a startup enriching HALEU fuel, Anthropic's new standard for AI-controlled lab/manufacturing hardware, and Hugging Face's robotics push amid a rumored $12.9B Nvidia acquisition.

insights.claim: The FDA approved Revolution Medicines' drug Rasonque, which targets the RAS protein mutation that drives runaway cell growth in pancreatic cancer, and in a late-stage study extended patient survival to more than 13 months versus about 6.7 months for chemotherapy alone.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A roughly 2x survival improvement in one of oncology's hardest-to-treat cancers is a strong data point for Revolution Medicines' RAS-targeting platform and validates the broader RAS-inhibitor drug class as investable.
insights.locator: FDA Approves Targeted Therapy for Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer

insights.claim: Rasonque received Breakthrough Therapy, Orphan Drug, and Priority Review designations and was reviewed under the FDA's Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program, resulting in approval about 6.5 months faster than the standard PDUFA review timeline.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Watch the National Priority Voucher pilot as a new regulatory accelerant — drugs that qualify can reach market roughly twice as fast as the normal accelerated pathway, compressing time-to-revenue for sponsors.
insights.quote: it was approved about 6.5 months faster than the standard PDUFA timeline
insights.locator: Per the Agency, "The FDA granted Rasonque Breakthrough Therapy

insights.claim: Former Nebraska Senator Ben Sasse, a trial participant who reported a significant reduction in his tumors, still expects to eventually die from his cancer even after treatment, illustrating that the drug buys time rather than delivering a cure.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Sets realistic expectations for the drug's commercial and clinical ceiling: it is a survival-extension therapy with visible side effects, not a cure, which should temper valuation multiples built on curative framing.

insights.claim: Drone startup Airbound, founded by a self-taught engineer from India who learned physics and engineering from YouTube during COVID, raised $37M from investors including Greenoaks and Lachy Groom.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A $37M round from Greenoaks signals institutional conviction in a founder-led drone startup despite a crowded field that already includes Zipline, suggesting differentiated technology or go-to-market.
insights.locator: Airbound Announces $37M Raise and Drops Manifesto

insights.claim: Airbound's founder published a manifesto arguing for a future where all movement happens in the air, positioning drones as a general logistics/mobility layer rather than a niche delivery product.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If aerial movement becomes a general mobility thesis rather than just last-mile delivery, it broadens the addressable market and potential exits for drone infrastructure startups beyond current logistics comps like Zipline.
insights.quote: the future where all movement is in the air
insights.locator: he did a great job laying out

themes.theme: Nuclear Microreactors Win Army Janus Program

insights.claim: The US Army selected five companies, including Radiant Nuclear and Antares Nuclear, for its $2.2B Janus program to deploy nuclear microreactors, with Radiant receiving $750M to build 15 Kaleidos microreactors and Antares reporting a contract value "on the order of $1B" and growing.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A $2.2B defense program validates microreactor unit economics and gives Radiant and Antares government-backed revenue and credibility that could de-risk future commercial and defense contracts.
insights.locator: Radiant and Antares Selected for US Army Janus Program

insights.claim: Over 55% of US soldier casualties in the two Iraq conflicts came from ambushes on convoys that were transporting ammunition, water, and fuel, meaning a reactor sited at a forward location could eliminate the need for many fuel shipments and, per the argument, save tens of thousands of lives.
insights.speaker: Doug (quoted by Packy McCormick)
insights.so_what: This casualty-reduction logic is the core strategic case the Pentagon is buying into for forward-deployed microreactors — a durable, mission-critical demand driver independent of commercial nuclear economics.
insights.quote: Over 55% of US soldier casualties in the two Iraqi conflicts are from ambushed convoys. And convoys move ammo, water, and fuel.
insights.locator: As Doug said in the deep dive

insights.claim: Antares Nuclear's co-founder Julia DeWahl previously co-hosted the Age of Miracles podcast with the article's author, an existing personal/professional connection disclosed in the piece.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Signals a personal network relationship between the author and Antares' leadership, relevant context for weighing the enthusiasm of this coverage.
insights.locator: whose co-founder Julia DeWahl was my Age of Miracles co-host

insights.claim: The author's portfolio company Standard Nuclear signed a binding agreement to supply Antares Nuclear with TRISO fuel through 2035 for microreactors built for defense and space missions, making it a supplier to both Janus-winning startups.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A single fuel supplier locking in long-term contracts with both Army-selected microreactor vendors positions Standard Nuclear as a picks-and-shovels play on the entire Janus program, not just one winner.
insights.locator: our portfolio company Standard Nuclear has signed a binding agreement

insights.claim: Actinide became the first startup to enrich uranium and produce HALEU (High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium), the fuel used inside TRISO pellets for many advanced reactors, using its Texas-built particle accelerator called Endurance.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A private startup achieving HALEU enrichment breaks a long-standing bottleneck (limited domestic HALEU supply) that has constrained the entire US advanced-reactor and microreactor supply chain, including Radiant and Antares.
insights.locator: Actinide Becomes First Startup to Enrich Uranium to HALEU

insights.claim: The same Endurance accelerator that now produces HALEU had, just the prior month, been producing enriched Yb-176, a precursor for cancer therapies worth roughly $30,000 per gram, as part of Actinide's stated goal of producing many isotopes to address atomic control broadly.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A single accelerator platform serving both nuclear fuel and high-value medical isotope markets suggests a diversified, capital-efficient business model rather than a single-product nuclear-fuel bet.
insights.quote: enriched Yb-176, a precursor for cancer therapies worth roughly $30,000 per gram

themes.theme: Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard for Lab and Manufacturing AI

insights.claim: Anthropic launched a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a protocol enabling AI agents to safely operate multiple physical lab and manufacturing instruments in parallel, such as microscopes, liquid handlers, and robotic arms, for tasks ranging from routine drug-discovery experiments to laser calibration on quantum computers.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A standardized interface for AI-to-lab-hardware control could become the equivalent of a driver/API layer for physical science automation, positioning Anthropic to capture value beyond software into physical R&D workflows.
insights.quote: a new standard for AI agents to safely operate physical equipment in scientific research and advanced manufacturing.
insights.locator: Anthropic Kicks Off Preview for Model Hardware Standard

insights.claim: The framing for MHS is that automating routine, tedious tasks like laser alignment frees humans to focus on higher-order scientific work, which the author treats as core to human purpose rather than a threat to scientist jobs.
insights.speaker: Ruxandra Teslo (referenced by Packy McCormick)
insights.so_what: This framing — AI absorbing rote lab work rather than replacing scientists — is the narrative likely to shape how AI-in-science tools get adopted and defended against automation-anxiety pushback.
insights.locator: Ruxandra Teslo has some good quick thoughts here

insights.claim: David Hansen reported that at his company Westmag, Claude and Codex were used by hardware engineers in 2026 to vibe-code the microcontrollers and tablets running the MES, ERP, and inline/end-of-line testing systems used to set up US manufacturing operations.
insights.speaker: David Hansen (quoted by Packy McCormick)
insights.so_what: A concrete, named example of AI coding tools being used to stand up real manufacturing infrastructure (not just prototypes) is evidence that AI-assisted reshoring of US manufacturing is already operational, not theoretical.
insights.quote: I couldn’t overstate how important Claude and Codex have been for setting up manufacturing in the USA in 2026

themes.theme: Hugging Face's Nvidia Deal and Microduck Robot

insights.claim: Rumors circulated that Nvidia would acquire Hugging Face, the open-source model repository, for $12.9 billion, which the author frames as consistent with Nvidia's strategy of commoditizing complementary software layers to drive hardware demand.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If confirmed, a $12.9B deal would be one of the largest AI-infrastructure acquisitions of the year and would put the dominant open-source model hub under Nvidia's umbrella, a major supply-chain consolidation signal to watch.
insights.locator: rumors swirled that Nvidia would be buying Hugging Face

insights.claim: Hugging Face co-founder Thomas Wolf teased major news on Twitter/X with "We have a huge news to share today!", but the announcement turned out to be the launch of Microduck, a new robot from Pollen Robotics, rather than confirmation of the Nvidia deal.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The mismatch between market expectation (acquisition confirmation) and actual announcement (a robotics product) suggests the Nvidia deal remains unconfirmed speculation, not yet a completed transaction to price in.
insights.quote: We have a huge news to share today!
insights.locator: Thomas Wolf tweeted on Thursday morning

insights.claim: Pollen Robotics, acquired by Hugging Face in 2025, launched Microduck, a $399 reinforcement-learning-trainable robot that can walk, sit, crouch, roller-skate, pick up objects with its articulated beak, and recover on its own out of the box.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A sub-$400 consumer-accessible RL robot with capable out-of-box behavior could seed a hobbyist/education robotics ecosystem for Hugging Face similar to how open model weights built its ML community, a potential distribution wedge into physical AI.
insights.quote: walk, sit, crouch, roller-skate, pick up objects with its articulated beak, and recover on its own.
insights.locator: it can do a bunch of stuff out of the box
